methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Roanoke College partners with Google for free AI training - WDBJ7
signals.signal_reading: Google-partnered free AI training at Roanoke College creates distributed skill-building infrastructure beyond NoVA, potentially seeding peer learning networks in traditionally underserved regions if adoption scales beyond institutional boundaries.

signals.title: Norfolk native brings free AI workshops to Hampton Roads to close the technology gap - WTKR
signals.signal_reading: Norfolk native bringing free AI workshops directly to Hampton Roads demonstrates grassroots capability distribution aimed at closing technology gaps, signaling potential for community-driven deep learning rather than platform-dependent adoption.

signals.title: New partnership between VCU and AI Ready RVA aims to boost AI education, innovation and community impact - VCU News
signals.signal_reading: VCU-AI Ready RVA partnership concentrates institutional AI capability in Richmond's metro core, creating a secondary excellence hub that could either distribute outward or deepen the metro-rural divide depending on community reach design.

signals.title: George Mason student teaches DC-area seniors how to spot AI scams
signals.signal_reading: George Mason student teaching seniors AI scam detection represents shallow, defensive AI literacy concentrated in NoVA—users learning to navigate AI threats rather than building capability, signaling platform-dependent adoption patterns.

signals.title: Column: AI is reshaping Hampton Roads before our eyes - The Virginian-Pilot
signals.signal_reading: Opinion piece acknowledging AI reshaping Hampton Roads signals awareness of concentrated transformation in the defense-tech corridor, but commentary without accompanying workforce infrastructure suggests observation rather than distributed capability building.
